title: Feuerbach's Theorem: Wiedijk #29
content: Feuerbach's Theorem (1822): the nine-point circle of any triangle is internally tangent to the incircle and externally tangent to all three excircles. The nine-point circle passes through 9 special points: midpoints of the three sides, feet of the three altitudes, and midpoints of segments from vertices to the orthocenter. Its radius is $R/2$ (half the circumradius) and its center $N$ is the midpoint of the orthocenter $H$ and circumcenter $O$.
mathContext: The nine-point circle $(N, R/2)$ satisfies $d(N, I) = |R/2 - r|$ (internal tangency with incircle) and $d(N, I_k) = R/2 + r_k$ (external tangency with each excircle $k \in \{a,b,c\}$). The tangent point with the incircle is the Feuerbach point $F$.

title: Feuerbach Distance Relations (Proved)
content: Four theorems establishing the key distance relations for Feuerbach's theorem. The distance from the nine-point center $N$ to the incenter $I$ equals $|R/2 - r|$ (internal tangency with the incircle), and the distance from $N$ to each excenter $I_k$ equals $R/2 + r_k$ (external tangency with each excircle). All four are proved by direct coordinate computation delegated to FeuerbachsTheoremOQ01.
mathContext: The core relations: $d(N, I) = |R/2 - r|$ establishes internal tangency with the incircle, and $d(N, I_k) = R/2 + r_k$ for $k \in \{a,b,c\}$ establishes external tangency with each excircle. These follow from Euler's identity $OI^2 = R^2 - 2Rr$ and the relation $N = (O+H)/2$.

title: Feuerbach Tangency Theorems
content: Four theorems restating the distance relations as tangency conditions. The nine-point circle is internally tangent to the incircle ($d(N,I) = |R/2 - r|$) and externally tangent to each of the three excircles ($d(N,I_k) = R/2 + r_k$). The tangent point with the incircle is the Feuerbach point.
mathContext: Internal tangency: $d(c_1, c_2) = |r_1 - r_2|$ means the circles touch at exactly one point, with the smaller circle inside the larger. External tangency: $d(c_1, c_2) = r_1 + r_2$ means the circles touch at exactly one point, each outside the other.

title: Feuerbach's Theorem: Complete Statement
content: The complete theorem combining all four tangency results into a single conjunction: the nine-point circle is (1) internally tangent to the incircle ($d(N,I) = |R/2 - r|$) and (2-4) externally tangent to each excircle ($d(N,I_k) = R/2 + r_k$). Each part follows directly from the corresponding proved distance relation. This is Wiedijk's Theorem #29.
mathContext: The full statement: $d(N,I) = |R_9 - r| \wedge \bigwedge_{k \in \{a,b,c\}} d(N, I_k) = R_9 + r_k$. The proof is a 4-tuple of the distance theorems. The tangent point with the incircle is the Feuerbach point $X(11)$ in Kimberling's notation.

title: Equilateral Triangle Special Case
content: For an equilateral triangle with side $s$: $R = 2r$ (circumradius equals twice the inradius). This means $R/2 = r$, so the nine-point circle has the same radius as the incircle and they coincide. The internal tangency degenerates to coincidence: $d(N,I) = |R/2 - r| = 0$. Proved by coordinate computation via FeuerbachsTheoremOQ01.
mathContext: For an equilateral triangle: $R = 2r$, $R_9 = R/2 = r$, and $N = I$ (all centers coincide). The Feuerbach tangency becomes $d(N,I) = |r - r| = 0$, confirming coincidence. The equilateral triangle is the unique triangle where all excircles have equal radii: $r_a = r_b = r_c$.
